cli.about: Policy-enforcing relay for AI agents: git over SSH, GitHub API over HTTP
cli.config: Configuration file (shared with the Python gateway)
cli.needs_relay: Exit 0 if a git-relay handler is configured, 1 if not, 2 if the configuration is invalid (for entrypoint.sh)
cli.serve: Start the SSH (git), HTTP (API) and 443 passthrough listeners
cli.login: Authenticate to the upstream with the device flow and store the token and known_hosts
cli.login.upstream: Upstream to log in to (git-relay domain). Defaults to the default upstream; used with several upstreams
cli.upstream: Upstream (git-relay domain). Defaults to the default upstream
cli.whoami: Show which upstream identity the relay acts as
cli.check: Show the resolved policy and state (agent / known_hosts / token / keys)
cli.unlock: Unlock the secret store (prompts; sets the passphrase the first time)
cli.unlock.stdin: Read the passphrase from stdin as one line instead of prompting (what mise run gw:unlock-auto pipes into). Refused at a terminal
cli.lock: Forget the secret store's key until it is unlocked again
cli.passphrase: Change the secret store's passphrase (prompts for the old one and the new)
cli.passphrase.kdf: argon2id (default) | pbkdf2-sha256. PBKDF2 is what FIPS approves and is weaker against GPUs for the same passphrase
cli.store_status: Whether the secret store is unlocked, locked, or not initialised
cli.proxy_credential: The upstream proxy's credential, kept in the secret store instead of a file the agent can read
cli.proxy_credential.set: Store the username and password (prompts; never an argument, which would reach ps)
cli.store_export: Write the secret store as a sealed envelope to stdout (no passphrase; works while locked)
cli.store_export.out: Write to this file instead of stdout, created 0600
cli.store_import: Replace an empty secret store with an envelope read from stdin
cli.store_import.file: Read from this file instead of stdin
cli.revoke.label: Token label as shown by `tokens`
cli.revoke_project: Revoke every token of the project (when the project ends)
cli.add_key: Register a disposable SSH public key by hand (one OpenSSH line, or --file)
cli.add_key.file: Read the public key from this file
cli.keyscan: Fetch the host keys of an upstream or a ProxyJump bastion with ssh-keyscan and append them to that upstream's known_hosts (shows fingerprints)
cli.keyscan.upstream: Which upstream's known_hosts to write to (git-relay domain). Defaults to the default upstream
cli.agent: Agent-side CLI (does not read the configuration file; uses SEKIMORE_ENDPOINT / SEKIMORE_TOKEN / SEKIMORE_REPO)
cli.agent.repo: Default repository Org/Repo (or host/Org/Repo with several upstreams)
agent.whoami: Show your project, permissions and repositories
agent.guide: Print the guide for AI agents (what the relay is, how to push, the sekimore commands, how to read denials)
agent.guide.lang: Language of the guide (en / ja). Defaults to SEKIMORE_LANG / LANG
agent.project: Projects v2 operations (the relay builds the GraphQL)
agent.repo.vocabulary: List the labels, assignable people and open milestones this repository defines
agent.search: Search issues and pull requests across the project's repositories
agent.search.query: Query in GitHub's search syntax (e.g. "is:open label:bug"). The project's repositories are added to it
agent.release.create: Create a release for a tag that already exists upstream (push the tag first)
agent.release.view: Show the release for one tag
agent.release.edit: Edit a release, or publish a draft (--draft false)
agent.release.edit.draft: true keeps it a draft, false publishes it (publishing needs release:publish)
agent.release.edit.prerelease: true marks it a prerelease, false takes the mark off
agent.release.title: Title (defaults to the tag name)
agent.release.notes: Body text (write --notes="…" when it starts with -)
agent.release.notes_file: Read the body from this file
agent.release.generate_notes: Have GitHub write the notes from the pull requests since the previous tag. This is the default when no body is given, and with a body the generated notes are appended
agent.release.draft: Create it as a draft, so a human publishes it
agent.pr.create.head: Head branch (e.g. sekimore/topic)
agent.pr.create.title: Title
agent.pr.merge.method: Merge method: merge / squash / rebase (default: the repository's own)
agent.pr.merge.title: Title of the merge commit
agent.pr.merge.message: Body of the merge commit (write --message="…" when it starts with -)
agent.pr.merge.delete_branch: Delete the head branch once the merge succeeded
agent.pr.update: Edit a pull request: title, body or base branch
agent.pr.update.title: New title
agent.pr.update.body: New body (write --body="…" when it starts with -)
agent.pr.update.base: New base branch (it has to be one of the repository's allowed bases)
agent.pr.status: Show the state of a pull request and its CI checks
agent.pr.status.json: Print raw JSON (default: one-line summary plus the check list)
agent.pr.request_review: Ask people to review a pull request
agent.pr.team_reviewers: Teams to ask, comma separated (the slug, without the organization)
agent.pr.view: Show one pull request: title, body, branches and the counts
agent.pr.comments: Show everything said on a pull request: the conversation, the reviews and the comments on the diff
agent.pr.list.base: Only pull requests against this base branch
agent.issue.view: Show one issue: title, body, labels and assignees
agent.issue.comments: Show the comments on an issue
agent.issue.list: List issues (pull requests are left to pr list)
agent.issue.list.labels: Only issues carrying all of these labels, comma separated
agent.issue.list.assignee: Only issues assigned to this login
agent.comments.limit: How many to fetch from each source (default 30)
agent.pr.files: Which files a pull request touches, and how much changed in each
agent.pr.diff: Read one file of the diff, with the line numbers a line comment is addressed by
agent.diff.path: Which file to read. Without one, the first file of the pull request
agent.diff.window: How many diff lines to show (default 400)
agent.diff.before: Start at this line of the file's patch (the previous page's end)
agent.security: Dependabot alerts: what is vulnerable and what fixes it
agent.security.alerts: List the repository's Dependabot alerts, one line each (severity, package, manifest, advisory, first fixed version)
agent.security.dismiss: Set an alert aside with a reason. security:dismiss, not security:read — it makes a vulnerability stop being shown
agent.security.reopen: Put a dismissed alert back to open (same permission as dismiss)
agent.ci.runs: List workflow runs for a ref (tag / branch / SHA), e.g. the Docker Publish of a tag push
agent.ci.jobs: List the jobs of a run (which failed, job_id). --number (latest run of the PR) or --run-id (from ci runs)
agent.ci.rerun: Re-run a workflow run (the failed jobs by default)
agent.ci.rerun.all: Re-run every job, not only the ones that failed
agent.ci.cancel: Cancel a workflow run that is still going
agent.ci.log: Show a job log from the end. --before pages further back
agent.ci.log.number: PR number (the failed job of its latest run is selected)
agent.ci.log.run_id: Run ID (from ci runs; its failed job is selected)
agent.ci.log.window: Number of lines from the end (default 200)
agent.ci.log.before: Show lines before this line number (pass the start of the previous page)
agent.issue.title: Title
agent.issue.update: Correct an issue's title or body
agent.issue.label: Add labels to an issue
agent.project.add_item: Add an item to a project
agent.project.update_item: Update a field of a project item
agent.project.update_item.value: JSON, or a string (a string becomes {"text": …})
agent.project.project_id: Project node ID. --board names the same board without one
agent.project.board: Board number, as config.yml and the URL write it (github.com/users/<user>/projects/<n>). The default when the project has one board
agent.project.fields: List the board's fields and the option ids of every single-select (needed by update-item)
op.login.no_meta_keys: warning: GET /meta returned no ssh_keys; populate {path} with `docker compose exec sekimore-gw sekimore-relay keyscan <host>`
op.login.meta_failed: warning: could not fetch upstream ssh host keys ({error}); populate {path} with `docker compose exec sekimore-gw sekimore-relay keyscan <host>`
op.login.bastion_scan: the ProxyJump bastion {host}:{port} has no host key yet; taking it now
op.login.bastion_scan_failed: could not take the host keys of the bastion {host}:{port} ({error}). login stops here: the hop to the upstream cannot be made without them. Take them with `sekimore-relay keyscan {host} --port {port} --upstream {domain}` and log in again
op.login.bastion_check_failed: cannot tell whether the bastion {host}:{port} has a host key ({error}); login stops here
op.login.via_bastion_failed: could not take the host keys of {host}:{port} through the bastion ({error}). login stops here: git through the relay cannot work without them. Take them with `sekimore-relay keyscan {host} --port {port} --upstream {domain}` and log in again
op.login.keys_confirm: Add these host keys for {what} to known_hosts? [yes/no]
op.login.keys_not_interactive: not a terminal, so the host keys of {what} are left unsaved; run `sekimore-relay keyscan` for them from a terminal
op.login.keys_unreadable: warning: could not read the answer for {what} ({error}); the keys are left unsaved. Run `sekimore-relay keyscan` for them from a terminal, or `mise run gw:login` again
op.login.keys_required: the host keys of {host}:{port} were not saved, so login stops here: git through the relay cannot work without them. Run login again and answer yes, or take them without the question: `sekimore-relay keyscan {host} --port {port} --upstream {domain}`, then log in
op.whoami.note1: note: the gateway acts as this identity. GitHub cannot distinguish
op.whoami.note2: agent actions from yours — the gateway audit log is the only record.
op.keyscan.header: host keys of {host}:{port} — verify these fingerprints out of band before trusting them:
op.keyscan.none: ssh-keyscan returned no host keys for {host}:{port} ({stderr})
op.keyscan.via_bastion: {host}:{port} is behind a ProxyJump bastion ({bastions}); taking its host keys through it, one connection per key type
op.keyscan.via_bastion_none: no host keys came back for {host}:{port} through the bastion ({stderr})
op.keyscan.bastion_missing: the bastion {bastions} has no host key in this upstream's known_hosts, so the hop to the upstream cannot be made. Scan the bastion first. {remedy}
op.check.proxy_credential_locked: {state} — the secret store is locked; run: mise run gw:unlock
op.check.proxy_route_squid: via the local Squid (OpenSSL speaks TLS to the upstream)
op.check.proxy_egress_direct: direct egress allowed — dev's traffic to allow_domains bypasses the upstream (proxy.direct_egress: deny to force Squid)
op.check.proxy_reach_squid_peer: {state} — Squid ({endpoint}) could not reach the upstream proxy: {status}. Check proxy.upstream_proxy and its credential, and Squid's cache.log
op.check.proxy_handshake_hint: the upstream accepted none of the relay's cipher suites — it must offer TLS 1.3 or ECDHE (a Squid https_port needs tls-dh=prime256v1). Until it does, set upstream_proxy_tls: false, or see https://github.com/Amakata/sekimore-gw/issues/205
op.check.proxy_offers_none: (openssl is not in PATH; run openssl s_client -connect {endpoint} -servername {host} -brief on the host to see what the proxy offers)
op.check.deny_note: ([-] = project deny; wins over any allow)
op.check.upstreams: upstreams (layer between project defaults and repos):
op.check.repos: repos (effective = project defaults + upstream layer + repo allow - deny):
op.check.bastion_ok: bastion:         {host}:{port} {state} (the ProxyJump hop is held to this upstream's known_hosts)
op.check.bastion_missing: bastion:         {host}:{port} {state} — in the gateway: sekimore-relay keyscan {host} --port {port} --upstream {domain} (mise run gw -- keyscan …)
op.check.signing_off: none — the dev container generates its own (relay.signing_key)
op.check.signing_key_missing: signing key:     {state} — ssh-add {fingerprint} on the host; commits will not be signed
agent.pr.reply: Reply to a line comment, where it was left
agent.pr.reply.comment_id: The comment to answer, as `pr comments` prints it (#2451 -> 2451)
agent.pr.review.comment: A note on one line: path:line:body. Repeat for more than one
agent.pr.review.comments_file: A JSON file of notes: [{"path":…,"line":…,"body":…}], for bodies too long or awkward for --comment
agent.pr.draft: Put a pull request back to draft
agent.pr.create.draft: Open it as a draft: CI runs, nobody is asked to look yet
agent.ci.dispatch.ref: The branch or tag to run it on
agent.ci.dispatch.input: An input the workflow declares: key=value. Repeat for more
agent.pr.comment_edit: Correct a comment this agent posted
agent.pr.comment_delete: Withdraw a comment this agent posted
agent.comment_id: The comment, as `pr comments` prints it (#2451 -> 2451)
agent.comment_inline: It is a comment on a line of the diff, not in the conversation
agent.issue.comment_edit: Correct a comment this agent posted

sgw.about: sgw: operate a sekimore-gw project from the host — the gateway, the secret store, the dev container
sgw.project: the project (the directory that holds .devcontainer/); default: found from the current directory
sgw.no_tty: never allocate a terminal for docker exec
sgw.cmd.check: the relay's configuration and state (ssh-agent / known_hosts / upstream token / keys / tokens)
sgw.cmd.whoami: which GitHub identity the gateway acts as
sgw.cmd.login: log in to GitHub with the device flow (first time only; asks before saving a host key)
sgw.cmd.unlock: unlock the secret store (after every recreate; the first run sets the passphrase)
sgw.cmd.lock: forget the secret store's key (the GitHub API stops until the next unlock)
sgw.cmd.store_status: whether the secret store is unlocked, locked, or not initialised
sgw.cmd.passphrase: change the secret store's passphrase (--kdf pbkdf2-sha256 switches the KDF)
sgw.cmd.proxy_credential: the upstream proxy's credential, in the store: sgw proxy-credential set|clear
sgw.cmd.store_export: write the secret store out sealed: sgw store-export > store.json
sgw.cmd.store_import: replace an empty secret store with an envelope: sgw store-import < store.json
sgw.cmd.tokens: the project tokens that have been issued
sgw.cmd.revoke: revoke one token: sgw revoke --label skm_xxxxxxxx
sgw.cmd.revoke_project: revoke every token of the project
sgw.cmd.bootstrap: the kill-switch for automatic registration: sgw bootstrap disable|enable
sgw.cmd.keyscan: add the host key of an upstream or a bastion to known_hosts (through the bastion when the upstream has one)
sgw.cmd.relay: run any sekimore-relay subcommand in the gateway: sgw relay <subcommand> [args…]
sgw.cmd.unlock_auto: unlock the secret store with the passphrase this host has stored (Keychain / Secret Service / a root-owned file); exit 0 when there is none
sgw.cmd.keychain_set: store the secret store's passphrase in this host's own keychain, once, so that recreate unlocks by itself
sgw.cmd.recreate: pull the image compose declares and recreate the gateway on it (restart keeps the old one), then unlock the store when this host has the passphrase
sgw.cmd.restart: restart the gateway (after changing domain_handlers / relay in config.yml; dev keeps running)
sgw.cmd.logs.tail: how many lines to start with
sgw.cmd.audit: follow the relay's audit log (every denial and every operation; Ctrl-C to stop)
sgw.cmd.db_stats: rows, period, size and indexes of the gateway's log DB
sgw.cmd.db_prune: delete logs older than N days: sgw db-prune --before-days 90 --yes [--vacuum]
sgw.cmd.db_reset: empty the log DB and VACUUM: sgw db-reset --yes
sgw.cmd.reload_status: whether saving config.yml takes effect right now
sgw.cmd.reload_follow: open the reload window (30m by default): sgw reload-follow 1h
sgw.cmd.reload_freeze: close the reload window now (before handing work to an AI)
sgw.cmd.dev: a command in the dev container as the vscode user; none is a zsh
sgw.cmd.agent_setup: run agent-setup again in dev (registers the key with the relay and remakes the token and known_hosts)
sgw.cmd.signing_key: print the AI's signing public key (register it on GitHub as a Signing Key)
sgw.cmd.refresh: re-run the gateway's agent setup in dev, so the ~/.ssh/config Host blocks and the proxy environment follow config.yml without Rebuild Container
sgw.cmd.web: open the gateway's Web UI in a browser
sgw.cmd.ps: the containers of this project's compose stack
sgw.cmd.port: the host port a service publishes (default: container port 8080)
sgw.cmd.id: the container ID of a service
sgw.cmd.down: stop and remove the compose stack (the volumes stay)
sgw.cmd.open: start VS Code where the operator's SSH_AUTH_SOCK does not reach it
sgw.cmd.open.check: show the state of SSH_AUTH_SOCK in launchd, in Docker Desktop and in the running VS Code
sgw.cmd.open.restore: put SSH_AUTH_SOCK back into launchd (before restarting Docker Desktop)
sgw.inside: this is the inside of the dev container; run sgw on the host where Docker runs the stack
sgw.no_project: no project here: no .devcontainer/docker-compose.yml in {dir} or above it (use --project)
sgw.none: no running container for service '{service}' (is the devcontainer open? working_dir={dir})
sgw.several: several '{service}' containers are running; stop the others or say which project with --project:
sgw.needs_tty: {cmd} needs a terminal on stdin (do not pipe it)
sgw.no_port: service '{service}' publishes no host port for {port}
sgw.recreated: done. reload the Web UI's Relay tab (or run: sgw check)
sgw.recreate.left_locked: the store was left locked. Unlock it with: sgw unlock
sgw.recreate.unlock_failed: the gateway was recreated, but the automatic unlock failed. Unlock it with: sgw unlock
sgw.unlock_auto.none: no passphrase stored for '{project}' on this host{asked}. Store one with: sgw keychain-set   (or unlock by hand with: sgw unlock)
sgw.keychain.none: nothing was stored: the Keychain has no sekimore-gw entry for '{project}'
sgw.keychain.stored: {backend} now holds a passphrase for '{project}' ({n} characters). sgw recreate will use it
sgw.keychain.empty: an empty passphrase is not accepted; nothing was stored
sgw.keychain.mismatch: the two did not match; nothing was stored
sgw.keychain.readback: the Secret Service did not give back what was stored for '{project}'
sgw.keychain.no_backend:
this host has neither the macOS Keychain (security) nor a Secret Service (secret-tool), so there is nowhere to put it. On a server, use a root-owned file in {dir} instead (the host's own directory; do not mount it into the gateway):

  sudo install -d -m 0755 {dir}
  sudo systemd-creds encrypt --name=sekimore-gw - {dir}/{project}.passphrase.cred   (type the passphrase, then Ctrl-D)

or, without systemd-creds (the file itself is then the secret):

  sudo install -m 0600 /dev/null {dir}/{project}.passphrase
  sudo tee {dir}/{project}.passphrase >/dev/null   (type the passphrase and Enter, then Ctrl-D)

sgw unlock-auto reads either. SGW_PASSPHRASE_DIR names another directory
sgw.refresh.setup: == dev: run the gateway's agent setup again (the way post-start.sh does)
sgw.refresh.failed: sekimore-agent-setup.sh did not finish. Is the gateway up? (sgw check)
sgw.refresh.hosts: == dev: the Host blocks now in ~/.ssh/config
sgw.refresh.no_hosts: no sekimore-relay block in ~/.ssh/config: the gateway has no relay, or the setup wrote none
sgw.refresh.no_proxy: not present (no upstream proxy configured, or the gateway is older than 0.2.42)
sgw.refresh.proxy_present: present: a new shell in dev reads it; a shell already open needs . /etc/profile.d/sekimore-proxy.sh
sgw.refresh.done: refresh: done. The Host blocks apply at once; open a new terminal in dev for the proxy environment
sgw.cmd.verify: the acceptance check of the project: the gateway's state, the signing key, the store, git / HTTPS / one API call through the relay from dev, the upstream proxy, the host-side rules
sgw.cmd.init: write the project template into a directory (the dev container, the gateway, config.yml, the host-side files) for this version
sgw.cmd.init.target: what the project is: devcontainer (the only one this version implements), later sbx, devcontainer/colima
sgw.cmd.init.force: overwrite the template's files when they exist (.env is never overwritten)
sgw.cmd.init.dir: the project directory (default: the current one)
sgw.init.exists: these files exist already: {files}. Move them away, or --force to overwrite the template's files (.env is kept)
sgw.init.unsupported: target {target} is not implemented in this version of sgw; devcontainer (on Docker Desktop) is
sgw.init.next:
next: edit .devcontainer/config/config.yml (allow_domains, the relay's repositories), then open the directory in VS Code (Reopen in Container), and on this host:
  sgw unlock      # set the store's passphrase
  sgw login       # the upstream token
  sgw verify      # the acceptance check
sgw.cmd.update: compare the project's gateway and base pins and .devcontainer/sgw/ with this sgw's version, and say what an update would change (changes nothing without --apply)
sgw.cmd.update.apply: move to this sgw's version: rewrite the tags, replace .devcontainer/sgw/, recreate the gateway after asking, unlock
sgw.cmd.update.sync: bring .devcontainer/sgw/ in line with the versions already pinned (after changing a tag by hand, or the language)
sgw.cmd.update.notes: print the UPGRADING sections between the pinned versions and this sgw's
sgw.cmd.update.owned: only what your own files (mise.toml, devcontainer.json, …) need; no network
sgw.cmd.update.force: overwrite a distributed file that was edited by hand
sgw.cmd.update.offline: do not ask GHCR whether a release newer than this sgw exists
sgw.update.unpinned: {image} in {file} is not pinned to an X.Y.Z tag (latest, or a digest). Write a version there first
sgw.update.no_newest: could not ask GHCR for the newest {image} ({error}); going on with this sgw's version
sgw.update.registry: the registry of {image} is not supported (ghcr.io only)
sgw.update.newer_sgw: a newer release, {version}, is out; this sgw is {sgw}. Install it first: {install}
sgw.update.f_edited: edited by hand — applying stops here (--force overwrites)
sgw.update.lang_changed: language: {from} → {to} (the task files are taken again)
sgw.update.notes_hdr: UPGRADING, between the pinned and the newest versions (sgw update --notes prints them)
sgw.update.notes_none: UPGRADING: no release in between asks anything of you
sgw.update.next_edited: Restore the distributed files you edited, or move the change into mise.toml, before applying (or --force).
sgw.update.next_sgw: This sgw cannot write a newer version than its own. Install the newer sgw first: {install}
sgw.update.edited_stop: {file} has been edited by hand; overwriting it would lose that, so this stops.
sgw.update.edited_how: To change a task, define one with the same name in mise.toml (it wins over the include). Then restore this file with git checkout, or delete it, and run this again; or --force to overwrite it.
sgw.update.ask_recreate: Recreate the gateway on {version} now? Connections in use are dropped. [y/N]
sgw.update.owned_hdr: What your own files need (update does not write these)
sgw.update.owned_none: What your own files need: nothing
sgw.update.r_unlock: unlock the secret store: sgw unlock
sgw.update.r_gw_down: the gateway is not running; it comes up on {version} the next time it is opened (sgw open → Reopen in Container → sgw unlock)
sgw.update.r_rebuild: rebuild the dev container: Dev Containers: Rebuild Container from the VS Code command palette (base {version})
sgw.update.r_notes: read the UPGRADING sections: sgw update --notes
sgw.update.r_include: mise.toml does not take .devcontainer/sgw/ in. Put this into mise.toml:
sgw.update.r_poststart: make devcontainer.json's postStartCommand this one line (post-start.sh passes every SEKIMORE_* variable to sudo; the old --preserve-env= list goes):
sgw.update.r_commit: review the change and commit it: git diff
